newsitem.title: USA: INTERVIEW-Toro expects to make up Q1 shortfall.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW-Toro expects to make up Q1 shortfall.

text.p: Toro Co, which saw its fiscal first quarter earnings plunge to $0.20 a share from $0.67 last year, said Tuesday it expects to make up some of the dilution caused by its purchase of an irrigation products maker with a stronger showing in the second quarter.

"We think we're going to have a good second quarter, and basically be back on track for a solid fiscal 1997," Kendrick Melrose, Toro chairman and chief executive officer, told Reuters in a telephone interview. "We're looking at recovering virtually all or most of the deficit against plan," he said.

Last fall, Toro spent about $130 million to acquire James Hardie Irrigation Group from James Hardie Industries Ltd of Australia. The lawn care products and snowblower manufacturer said at the time it expected the deal to be slightly dilutive for the first year of the deal.

"The dilution (for the year) will be in the same range as we expected, between $0.20 and $0.24," Melrose said, adding that the company has already reduced that total by $0.12 or $0.13 a share in the first quarter alone.
For the first quarter ended January 31, Toro reported earnings of $2.5 million, down from $8.5 million one year ago.

"The bad news is that we ended up acquiring Hardie in the midst of their loss quarter," Melrose explained. "The good news is that we're getting some advance opportunity to get integrated so that when the next fiscal year comes, the acquisition costs, absorption, severance, and organizational changes will have been all done by then."
"Fiscal 1998 should be nicely accretive and the dilution will be all behind us," he said.
Melrose said Toro, which will hold its annual meeting Thursday, has an acquisition strategy in place that didn't exist a few years ago, when it focused on internal growth.
"We see our need to be broader and more comprehensive in how we serve our markets," Melrose said. "So we adopted a much more aggressive acquisition and joint venture strategy about three years ago."
Melrose said Toro has identified possible acquisition targets, but he added the company is not ready to take steps toward another deal in light of the debt associated with the Hardie deal.

Melrose also said he was comfortable with analysts' estimates for the second quarter of the year falling in the range of $1.50 and $1.55 a share. Analysts expect Toro to earn between $3.00 and $3.15 for all of fiscal 1997, Melrose said.

"I think we'll be comfortable we're going to be in that range (in the second quarter)," Melrose said. "I'm hopeful we'll do a little better, particularly if we can pick up a few cents we lost in the first quarter."
Toro shares closed unchanged Tuesday at 34-1/8.
